newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Statement from Swedish ruling party on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Statement from Swedish ruling party on EMU.

text.p: Following are extracts from a statement made by the executive committee of Sweden's ruling Social Democrat Party on the European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"Europe definitely looks different today compared with that point in time in the early nineties when the EMU process started. The conditions have changed.

"The single currency also entails further political integration between the member states. The co-operation will be deepened and widened, which the majority of our fellow social democratic parties in Europe see as a precondition for the enlargement of the EU to Eastern and Central European countries.
"At the same time, many warning voices have also been raised against EMU from social democrats as well as from economists and independent researchers.
"It has been pointed out that the EU lacks the labour mobility found in the U.S., for example. This in turn could lead to rising unemployment in certain regions when EMU is achieved.

"In view of the weak support for EMU among the Swedish people, Swedish participation in the monetary union when it starts on January 1, 1999 is not to be considered. The credibility of the Swedish political system would be seriously questioned if the Riksdag (Swedish parliament) decided on this major step in the autumn. At the same time the EU and Sweden's membership in the EU could be questioned even more. To this can be added doubts about the consequences of Swedish membership in the monetary union for Swedish economic development. "However in this context, the Board wants to emphasise that such a position must not lead to lowered ambitions with respect to the requirement for the balance in government finances, sustained low inflation and a better functioning wage formation. The consolidation of government finances which the government and the Social Democrats in the Riksdag have achieved was necessary, quite apart from Swedish membership in the EU and the possible participation in the monetary union.
